builder_plan.scenario: Tool errors or unavailable services cause your agent to abandon recoverable tasks.
builder_plan.change: Inject repeatable tool failures and change only the recovery policy.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current retry and fallback behavior under the same injected failures.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Recovered tasks, duplicate side effects, retries, time to recovery, and total cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: What Does "Now" Mean to Your Computer-Use Agent? Stale Screenshots, Page Loads, and Which Check to Run Before a Click
summary: Replaces blind reliance on fixed wait heuristics (and expensive frontier-model re-checks) with a network-idle wait of about one second plus a targeted pre-click pixel comparison before irreversible or loading-page actions. Costs roughly one extra screenshot comparison per guarded click—one eighth the latency of a frontier VLM check—and a small engineering effort to add wait rules and a break-even check policy. Can fail on pages with prolonged loading or continuous layout shifts (52% of commercial pages shifted within 6.5s after a 3s-capped network-idle wait), where a pixel match may confirm a stale frame or no stable state exists.
rationale: The authors show a one-second network-idle wait removes most staleness risk and a cheap pixel check matches frontier-model accuracy at one eighth the latency, so constrained-infrastructure teams can adopt it immediately with negligible cost.
technique: Pre-click staleness verification for GUI agents

claims.statement: Replaces blind reliance on fixed wait heuristics (and expensive frontier-model re-checks) with a network-idle wait of about one second plus a targeted pre-click pixel comparison before irreversible or loading-page actions. Costs roughly one extra screenshot comparison per guarded click—one eighth the latency of a frontier VLM check—and a small engineering effort to add wait rules and a break-even check policy. Can fail on pages with prolonged loading or continuous layout shifts (52% of commercial pages shifted within 6.5s after a 3s-capped network-idle wait), where a pixel match may confirm a stale frame or no stable state exists.

A pixel comparison verifies the click target's position as accurately as a frontier vision-language model at one eighth of the latency; a 4B model matches the frontier model at verifying action success.
